2607.11787.title: Forgetting Our Way to Shared Meaning: Effects of Forgetting on Conceptual Alignment in a Non-Partnership Coordination Game
2607.11787.paper_summary: Shared meaning in language requires people to learn and agree on categories. We ask how characteristics of agents' memories change the emergence and evolution of shared meaning. Without a coordination game, models of conceptual semantics cannot explain how shared meaning emerges and changes in groups of people; however, existing games assume that players share payoffs in a partnership setting. We model conceptual alignment as a non-partnership game and illustrate differences in actual and perceived conceptual convergence from counterfactual simulations using agents with varying levels of adaptiveness and memory degradation. We found that adaptive players achieved actual convergence faster and had closer final conceptual regions than non-adaptive players, while non-adaptive players perceived convergence earlier. Weighing novel information less over time resulted in more stable agreements than fixing the weight of novel information. Memory features are critical to the emergence and evolution of actual and perceived convergence.
2607.11787.paper_summary_zh: 共享語言的意義需要人們學習並同意分類。我們探討代理人的記憶特徵如何改變共享意義的出現和演變。沒有協調遊戲，概念語義的模型無法解釋共享意義如何在一群人中出現和變化；然而，現有的遊戲假設玩家在夥伴關係中共享收益。我們將概念對齊建模為非夥伴關係遊戲，並通過使用具有不同適應性和記憶衰退水平的代理進行反事實模擬，說明實際和感知概念收斂的差異。我們發現，適應性玩家比非適應性玩家更快達成實際收斂，並且最終的概念區域更接近，而非適應性玩家則較早感知到收斂。隨著時間的推移，對新資訊的權重降低導致比固定新資訊的權重更穩定的協議。記憶特徵對實際和感知收斂的出現和演變至關重要。
